### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`, touching **2** documentable anchor(s).

**1** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/concepts/metadata-lifecycle.mdx`  _(via ObjectStackProtocolImplementation (symbol, a top-level class))_

⛔ **2** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v16.mdx`  _(via ObjectStackProtocolImplementation (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-0.mdx`  _(via ObjectStackProtocolImplementation (symbol, a top-level class))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **11** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 8a83cebc15a5efedff290e2c208abfba08fca9d6` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `84c5b781b5fa7d2e9c5d6aee86def481eb990b18` — the merge of head `de14c8521a5d09a39d85476fa8434f9632b5be5a` into base `8a83cebc15a5efedff290e2c208abfba08fca9d6`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 84c5b781b5fa7d2e9c5d6aee86def481eb990b18 && git checkout 84c5b781b5fa7d2e9c5d6aee86def481eb990b18
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 8a83cebc15a5efedff290e2c208abfba08fca9d6 de14c8521a5d09a39d85476fa8434f9632b5be5a && git checkout -B drift-repro 8a83cebc15a5efedff290e2c208abfba08fca9d6 && git merge --no-ff de14c8521a5d09a39d85476fa8434f9632b5be5a

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 8a83cebc15a5efedff290e2c208abfba08fca9d6
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 8a83cebc15a5efedff290e2c208abfba08fca9d6` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `de14c8521a5d09a39d85476fa8434f9632b5be5a`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.duplicate-package-install-refusal.test.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.duplicate-package-target-namespace.test.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.install-manifest-id.test.ts, .changeset/24041-duplicate-install-refusal.md + packages/objectql/src/registry.ts (`SchemaRegistry.installPackage`, `NamespaceConflictError`, `unregisterItem`, `unregisterNamespace`), packages/objectql/src/security-catalog-namespace.ts, packages/objectql/src/default-record-page.ts, docs/adr/0048-cross-package-metadata-collision.md (Phase 1), packages/runtime/src/domains/packages.ts (`requireDuplicableSource`, the duplicate door), packages/runtime/src/http-dispatcher.ts (`errorFromThrown`), packages/types/src/thrown-http-error.ts (`resolveThrownHttpError`), packages/spec/src/api/package-lifecycle.zod.ts (`DuplicatePackageResponseSchema`), packages/services/service-package/src/index.ts (`publish`), packages/metadata-core/src/protocol-handshake.ts (`assertProtocolCompat`), packages/client/src/index.ts (`packages.duplicate`), scripts/check-durability-degradation-log-level.mjs (`FAILURE_PROPAGATION_SITES`), scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs, scripts/check-adr-0087-registration.mjs, and objectui at the pinned `f8267df93` (read only): packages-io.ts, PackagesPage.tsx, BuilderLanding.tsx.

Read at 2026-10-17, against the head named above. Inputs: card #24041's body and its five comments (`6225499409`, `6226147624`, `6226977409`, `6227008947`, `6227604127`); contract record `6224173098` on PR #24028 (flag 3); PR #24081's body (the round-2 rewrite), its 5-file list and the net diff `8a83cebc1..de14c8521` (+274/-14; `main` has not touched any of the five files since the merge base); and the 47 check-runs on the head, read last. Code read with `git show` at the head; line numbers below are the head's. Nothing built, run or re-run.

### ① Derived judgments

**The one accept-set change, and it is right.** `duplicatePackage` (`protocol.ts:27440-27489`) installs the copy's package record through `installPackage` before its copy loop. On `main` the call sat in `catch {}` and the loop ran regardless. At this head the catch logs once and rethrows `e` unchanged, so every duplicate whose `installPackage` throws is refused before any item is written, with the install's own object. No new judge is added, no sentence is reworded, and the `try` body (the `dupManifest` spread, `delete dupManifest.scope`, the call) can throw nothing but the install's refusal, so the accept set shrinks by exactly `installPackage`'s refusal set. **No false refusal.**

**Which duplicates that succeeded on `main` are refused now, and with what:**
- An explicit `targetNamespace` that a different installed package owns (shareable `base`/`system`/`sys` exempt; the ADR-0130 co-owner exemption never applies, there is no artifact scope): **422 `NAMESPACE_CONFLICT`**, `NamespaceConflictError`'s full sentence with its remedy (`registry.ts:1590-1620`, thrown at `:5494-5509`). Right: ADR-0048 Phase 1's install-time gate refuses exactly this, and on `main` the copy's objects were planted in the other package's namespace (the dev's round-1 probe).
- A derived namespace (`deriveNamespaceFromPackageId(targetPackageId)`, `:27136`) equal to another installed package's, the source's own included (`com.a.crm` duplicated to `com.b.crm`): the same 422. Right: on `main` that duplicate left a record-less copy plus per-object ADR-0029 D9.9 failures.
- A failed `sys_packages` write: **500**, `packagePersistFailureError`'s sentence (`:31628-31640`), which quotes only the package id and carries the store's answer on `cause`. Right: on `main` the items were copied for a package whose record never persisted.
- Reachable only by an in-process caller handing a collection-bearing record: the security-catalog and default-record-page conflicts (422, the registry's own sentences) and the ADR-0087 D1 handshake (`ProtocolIncompatibleError`, 422, `protocol-handshake.ts:122-128`). Each is a refusal `installPackage` already makes; rethrowing it is right. The `manifest.id` leg is unreachable (`duplicatePackage` parses `targetPackageId` with the same declaration first, `:27079-27085`).
- Unchanged, as the amendment ordered: a source with no registry record (`srcPkg` undefined) skips the install silently (`:27440`).

**Nothing left behind (premise 1): holds, by code read.** From the method head to the install call: `refuseOrganizationScopedWrite` (throws only, `:27050`, `:17362-17365`); two `safeParse` declarations (`:27079`, `:27136`); `registry.getPackage` (a read, `:27089`); `findEnvironmentRows('sys_metadata', …)` (`:27158`), which is `engine.find` plus `legacyOrganizationRowsOf`, a driver read (`:10432-10447`); then in-memory `Map`s and closures only (`renameMap`, `claimedBy`, `refusedObjects`, `viewItemRenames`, `deepRewrite`, `rewriteFieldRuleKeys`, `:27163-27437`). `copied`/`failed` and `resolveFlowCanonicalizer` sit after the install (`:27492-27497`). No mint, no `sys_metadata` row, no registry entry and no namespace owner precedes the call, so a rethrow needs no rollback.
- Inside `installPackage` on the 422 path: the registry's four judges (namespace gate, co-owned object names, security catalog, default record page) all run ahead of `registerNamespace`, `collection.set` and the two claim recorders (`registry.ts:5494-5611`), so a refused install leaves nothing. On the 500 path `undoInstall()` (`:31528-31551`) withdraws the row (`unregisterItem('package')`, `registry.ts:4880`) and releases the namespace only when this install registered it; the duplicate passes no `enableOnInstall`, so no lifecycle write happens.
- One residue, pre-existing and outside the claim: the undo does not call `forgetSecurityCatalogClaims`/`forgetDefaultRecordPageClaims`, so a 500 after `recordSecurityCatalogClaims`/`recordDefaultRecordPageClaims` (`:5607-5609`) leaves those claims. They read `positions`/`permissions`/`capabilities`/`pages` arrays (`security-catalog-namespace.ts:182`, `default-record-page.ts:109`), which a duplicable base's record manifest does not carry (the strict `ManifestSchema` at `POST /packages`, Studio and this door never write them), so from the HTTP door nothing is left. Reachable only in-process with a collection-bearing record and a failing `sys_packages` write. A #21243 seam in `installPackage`, which the claim bans editing; escalated in ③, not a FAIL here.

**The door: every refusal reaches the caller with the right status.** `POST /packages/:id/duplicate` (`runtime/src/domains/packages.ts:2152-2182`): `requireManageMetadata`, the walled-catalog refusal, `requireDuplicableSource` (422 `DUPLICATE_SOURCE_NOT_A_BASE` before the protocol call, `:628-660`), then `deps.errorFromThrown(e, 500)` on any throw. `errorFromThrown` (`http-dispatcher.ts:1237`) is `resolveThrownHttpError` (`thrown-http-error.ts`): it reads `.status`/`.statusCode`/`.code`, so `NamespaceConflictError` (`status` 422, registered code `NAMESPACE_CONFLICT`) answers `422 NAMESPACE_CONFLICT` with the registry's sentence and remedy intact, and the persist failure (`status` 500, no catalogued code) answers `500 INTERNAL_ERROR` with the primitive's sentence. `details` carries only a non-string code, `issues` or validation `fields`, never `cause`, and `this.error` withholds a leaky 5xx message besides (#3867): **no driver prose in any body.** The warn line is `console.warn` on the server; its string is the refusal's own sentence (a registry sentence, or the primitive's id-only sentence), and the error object is attached for a 5xx alone. Nothing a caller reads carries store prose.

**`OS_METADATA_COLLISION=warn`: the duplicate still proceeds, and that is right.** The gate is the registry's (`registry.ts:2328`, `:5498-5505`): under `warn` it logs and installs, `installPackage` returns, the copy becomes a second owner of the namespace and the loop runs. ADR-0048 Phase 1 names that downgrade as the documented deliberate-migration hatch; the PR inherits the gate's verdict instead of judging the namespace a second time, and the changeset says so under Remedy.

**The retired round-1 surface: gone.** No `type: 'package'` entry remains in `duplicatePackage` (the method's only `clientFacingFailureText(e, …)` is the per-item one, `:27657`); `copied`/`failed` are declared where `main` declares them (`:27492-27493`); the test file is rewritten to the refusal envelope; the changeset describes the refusal only. `FAILURE_PROPAGATION_SITES` still names `failed.push` as this function's declared sink (`check-durability-degradation-log-level.mjs:574-583`) and the diff leaves that sink exactly as declared; the gate concluded green in `Lint · docs & code guards`.

**The four comment edits are true at this head.** The docblock sentence; comment ① (a rethrown install refusal names `manifest.id`: `installPackage:31306-31312` throws `manifestIdRefusal('manifest.id', rawId)`); the target-namespace test ("the manifest write does not judge a namespace's charset at all": `protocol.installPackage` only derives a namespace when absent, `:31335-31338`; `SchemaRegistry.installPackage` carries no charset parse; `service-package.publish` serialises without parsing, `:479-495`); the manifest-id test ("would refuse the duplicate too, but under `manifest.id`").

**The pins hold the narrowing on both sides.** Case 1 asserts the thrown object is the registry's (`toBe`), resolves it through the door's own resolver to 422/`NAMESPACE_CONFLICT`, and asserts `saveMetaItem` never called, no target record, owners unchanged, one warn line with no error object. Case 2 stubs nothing on the install path: the `package` service returns `{ success: false, driverFault }`, `persistPackageManifest` reports it (`:31575-31590`), the real `undoInstall()` removes the row and the real 500 names the target and quotes nothing. The CONTROL copies and logs no refusal. The harness envelope matches the real class (`name`, `code`, `status` and `httpStatus` 422, the remedy clause). The dev's ablation (`throw e;` removed) reads both refusal cases red and the CONTROL green, the right direction.

### ② Semver level

- `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` on its own line in both the PR body and the changeset matches the diff: a published verb of `@objectstack/metadata-protocol` and the HTTP route built on it now refuse duplicates they accepted. AGENTS.md: `(narrowing)` is BREAKING; `check-changeset-no-major` (its docblock, `:58-96`, and the arm reading at `:1631-1670`): during the launch window a breaking change ships `minor`. **`"@objectstack/metadata-protocol": minor` is the right grade.** Bumping only that package is right: the runtime door's code is unchanged (its behaviour moves through the dependency) and `DuplicatePackageResponseSchema` is untouched.
- The ADR-0087 marker `adr-0087: not-required (no-migration-prescription)` is right: nothing stored, no spec key and no published type changes, so `objectstack migrate meta` has nothing to rewrite, and the body carries no FROM to TO prescription, the only thing the gate refuses that category on (`check-adr-0087-registration.mjs:147-155`). `Check Changeset` concluded success on both runs, the second after the body rewrite.
- The migration prose is true as read. Refused now: both legs, with "last segment of `targetPackageId`" a fair gloss of `deriveNamespaceFromPackageId`. Unchanged: an accepted install copies as before, per-item failures still ride `failed[]`, a record-less source still copies without one. Remedy: `targetNamespace` or another id, and the `warn` downgrade. Logged: as the code does.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **`open_questions`:** empty in round 2; round 1's question was answered by the amendment (ruling B) and built as ruled.
- **The `srcPkg`-undefined silent skip:** out of scope by the claim and kept out by the amendment ("The out-of-scope note stays out of scope"); the dev's "carrier: none" is right for this PR. Agreed it is a silent partial state of the same family: a copy with no package record, absent from `GET /packages`, which `requireDuplicableSource` lets through for an unknown id. **ESCALATED to the seat** as a candidate card (class b, reach unmeasured), the carrier the dev's note lacks.
- **The 4xx pin's harness stub at the registry boundary:** accepted. `@objectstack/objectql` depends on this package, so the real gate cannot be imported in-package; the harness throws the real class's envelope and the real `installPackage` meets it; objectql's five real-registry files that drive `duplicatePackage` passed in `Test Core` against the rebuilt `dist/`. The real-registry probes are cited, not kept, which the dependency cycle justifies.
- **The warn line attaching the error object for a 5xx:** right to keep the line, and attaching is harmless, but the stated reason is inaccurate at this head. For the real `package` service, `publish` logs the raw driver error itself at `error` (`service-package/src/index.ts:505`) and returns a constant sentence as `driverFault.message` (`PACKAGE_PUBLISH_DRIVER_FAULT_MESSAGE`, `:50-52`), so the thrown 500's `cause` carries no driver text; what the attachment adds is the duplicate's context, not the driver's words. The ruling's condition (keep the warn if the refusal is otherwise unlogged) is met: nothing else logs that the duplicate was refused. The pin's `DRIVER_TEXT` on `driverFault.message` models a shape the real service never emits; the assertion it carries (the primitive's sentence quotes nothing) still holds. Not a FAIL. A sibling asymmetry, noted not filed: `declaresClientRefusal` reads `status` alone (`:3597-3600`) while `packagePersistFailureError` passes through a 4xx declared by `statusCode`; such a refusal would get the error object on the server log line only.
- **The PR-body conflict the dev raised:** resolved. The body at review time carries `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` and ruling B (`updated_at` 2026-10-17T00:53:54Z, after the round-2 report), and the `Check Changeset` run that edit triggered concluded success. Nothing to escalate.
- **The dev's "ADR-0087 D1 not reachable in practice":** agreed; were it reached, the rethrown 422 `OS_PROTOCOL_INCOMPATIBLE` with its diagnostic would be the right answer.
- **`installPackage`'s undo and the two claim recorders** (① above): **ESCALATED to the seat** as a candidate card, class b, reach unmeasured and in-process only; it belongs to `installPackage` (#21243), which this claim bans editing.
- **Studio (premise 3):** holds at the pin. `packages-io.ts` `duplicatePackage` throws `readEnvelopeFailureText(payload)` on any non-OK answer (`:278-289`), and both callers show that message (`PackagesPage.tsx:584-588`, `BuilderLanding.tsx:140-141`); Studio sends no `targetNamespace`, so from Studio the conflict arrives only through a derived namespace, with the registry's remedy in the banner. The SDK's `packages.duplicate` goes through `unwrapResponse` (`client/src/index.ts:2987-3003`). No caller reads the partial copy.

**Check-runs on the head:** 47, every one completed: 39 success, 8 skipped (`Build Docs`, `Console Pin Gate`, the Dogfood shard matrix, `Dogfood Verify CLI`, `Packed-tarball smoke (opt-in)`, `Temporal Conformance (live PG + MySQL)`, and the second event run's `Auto Label` and `Check PR Size`). `Build Core`, `Test Core` and its six shards, `TypeScript Type Check`, `Lint & Repo Gates` and every `Lint ·` job, `Check Changeset` (twice), and `Governed Surface Queue Guard` are green. None is still running.
